evals.prompt: I added a `loading` prop to Button.tsx, can you sync it with the Figma registry?
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers. Agent runs fetch and extract-code, finds component-owned `loading` in shared `.figma/cache/code-props-cache.json`, does not invent a Figma binding when none exists, writes the matched artifact, finalizes the validated registry entry without a second export-name confirmation, then reports `loading` as unbound and omitted from durable codePropsMap.
expectations: The skill is invoked
extract-code (or fetch + extract-code) is run before any registry file is written
The agent does not claim an unbound code prop belongs in durable codePropsMap
The agent uses only shared `.figma/cache/code-props-cache.json` for code extraction and does not create `_code-props-raw.json`
The agent does not silently invent a mappingKind for the new prop
finalize writes the validated registry entry without a second export-name confirmation

evals.prompt: why does CI keep failing on the component-registry check for Checkbox
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers. Agent runs `check --components Checkbox` (or unscoped check), explains the stale codePropsMap drift found, and does not attempt to fix it by editing registry/*.json by hand.
expectations: The skill is invoked
check is run (scoped to Checkbox if possible)
The explanation names the specific stale field(s), not just 'something is stale'
No registry/*.json file is edited directly with Write/Edit

evals.prompt: does the Button component's Figma mapping still match the code
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers. Agent runs check and/or verify-source for Button and reports drift status. Agent does NOT run finalize on its own initiative — this is a read-only status question, not a sync request.
expectations: The skill is invoked
check or verify-source is run, scoped to Button where possible
finalize is not run in this turn
The agent reports match/mismatch clearly, e.g. citing codePropsMap or figmaBindings drift

evals.prompt: regenerate registry/ui/Button.json from the latest Figma file ABC123
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers. Agent runs the full pipeline: fetch (file-key ABC123) → extract-code → writes _figma-props-matched.json → finalize → scoped check → verify-source. Matching codeComponent values determine export names; no second confirmation is requested.
expectations: The skill is invoked
fetch is called with file-key ABC123
extract-code runs before finalize
finalize creates registry/ui/Button.json without asking for a second export-name confirmation
scoped check and verify-source run after finalize

evals.prompt: I love this Figma file's color palette, can you describe the style
evals.expected_output: Skill does NOT trigger. This is a general design/visual question with no code-props or registry sync intent.
expectations: The figma-component-registry skill is not invoked
No fetch/extract-code/finalize/check/verify-source command is run

evals.prompt: can you just edit registry/ui/Button.json directly to add a new binding
evals.expected_output: Near-miss. Skill triggers (or is at least consulted) but the agent declines to hand-edit the registry JSON with Write/Edit, and instead points to the CLI workflow (fetch/extract-code/finalize) as the supported way to add a binding.
expectations: The agent does not use Write or Edit on a registry/*.json file
The agent explains that registry files are generated by the CLI, not hand-edited
The agent offers the equivalent CLI path (fetch/extract-code + matched file + finalize) instead

evals.prompt: what does mappingKind bundle mean in our schema
evals.expected_output: Reference-level trigger. Agent answers from SKILL.md's mappingKind table / references/schema.md without running any CLI command — this is a documentation lookup, not a sync task.
expectations: The answer correctly describes bundle: one Figma value assigns several code props at once, requires props + valueProps
No fetch/extract-code/finalize/check/verify-source command is run for this request

evals.prompt: Our design-system Button is a Vue 3 SFC using defineProps, defineEmits, defineSlots, and defineModel. Add it to the registry.
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers from a Vue app/package root. Agent auto-detects Vue from package.json, extracts .vue files through vue-component-meta, keeps declared props and modelValue, excludes compiler-confirmed emits/listeners and global Vue props, preserves explicitly declared ARIA and composition-relevant props for review, then follows the normal fetch/match/finalize workflow without creating registry/config.json.
expectations: The skill auto-detects the Vue adapter from the app/package root and scans .vue files
No registry/config.json is created
Vue 3 defineProps and defineModel APIs are available as mapping candidates
defineEmits and defineSlots members do not enter codePropsMap candidates
The agent does not add Vue 2 or class-component compatibility
The same framework-neutral registry schema and finalize workflow are used

evals.expected_output: Explicit skill invocation plus a Figma component URL is write intent. Agent resolves matching code components, runs fetch → extract-code → match → finalize → scoped check → verify-source, and creates durable registry JSON without asking for export-name confirmation.
expectations: The explicit skill invocation is treated as authorization to write generated registry output
The Figma file key and node ID are parsed from the URL
Matching codeComponent values determine export names
finalize creates durable registry JSON without a second confirmation
scoped check and verify-source run for every finalized export
Exceptional mappings are reported after writing rather than used as a confirmation gate

evals.expected_output: Skill fetches Figma definitions and extracts code, but no matching code component exists. Agent stops before finalize, reports searched source scope and missing component, and does not invent an export or registry file.
expectations: fetch and extract-code run before declaring the code component missing
finalize is not run when no matching code component exists
No registry JSON is created for an invented export
The searched source scope and missing component are reported
